items.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: First I joined Cal Tjader on the West Coast, and then Ahmad Jamal, then I went from Ahmad Jamal to Count Basie.

ctx.x: You learn what not to play — I’m not going to play like that.

No, I’ve had many experiences. Ahmad Jamal, Errol Garner, Art Blakey, Count Basie, Ella Fitzgerald, Louis Armstrong, you know, it goes on and on, Charlie Mingus, you know, and Shearing. Dave Brubeck, he had that big hit when I was in high school. Ellington, everybody. I learned from everybody, you know? Ervin, Billy Eckstine, they were all you know, they were making music in those days. They were nice times. Even Theresa Brewer and Frankie Laine, I listened to them, you know? The Four Lads, The Platters, the…
